Definition: to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of, from want of memory or attention
BiblicalUsage: Shakach is to forget, and the Bible treats forgetting as a moral act, not a slip of memory. The chief butler forgot Joseph in prison, and Israel forgot the God who brought them out of Egypt, days without number. God answers the charge from both sides, promising He will not forget the covenant of the fathers, and asking whether a woman can forget her sucking child, yet He will not forget His people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe forgetting God is the root of every other sin, because a people that forgets its deliverer will invent a new one. The promise that He will not forget us is the anchor when our own memory fails. That is why I hold fast to His word, so that I do not forget what He has done.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; Moses; Isaiah; Jeremiah
